record_identity.title: Defensive Legitimacy Recognition and Cyber Incident Assistance Framework

summary: Proposal to establish a cross-domain CAM framework for recognising authorised defensive cybersecurity activity and preserving useful AI assistance during active incidents. The framework would require systems to distinguish interpretation and reconstruction of an existing attack pathway from operationalisation against a new or unauthorised target; verify defensive authority, affected-system relationship, purpose, scope, custody and execution boundaries; and prefer bounded safe continuation, confidential escalation and non-executing assistance over content-only denial.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Attack telemetry may contain the same exploit code, commands, credentials, malicious artefacts and infrastructure indicators that would appear in an offensive request. Content alone therefore cannot establish malicious intent. Where an authorised defender is blocked from interpreting compromise of an affected or lawfully administered system, safety controls may invert their protective purpose, delay containment and create dependency on exceptional provider access or locally controlled models. CAM already contains strong authority, source-separation, security, runtime, incident, audit and sovereign-assurance doctrine, but lacks one explicit positive framework connecting those elements to defensive cyber assistance.

It did not find one explicit positive doctrine requiring authority-aware defensive classification, a defensive-assistance posture, safe continuation after cyber-content gating, a provider escalation lane, cyber-specific forensic custody records or a transition rule from red-team evaluation into a real incident.

contextual_relations.rationale: PROP-0019 governs adversarial evaluation, capability cultivation, role confinement and artefact transfer. PROP-0021 governs authority-aware assistance during or after an actual cybersecurity incident. A red-team event that escapes containment should transition from the PROP-0019 evaluation pathway into the incident lifecycle proposed here.
Adversarial policy laundering through delegation remains distinct from denial of legitimate defensive assistance, but both require model, role, permission, telemetry and action provenance.

migration_notes: Individual records maintain canonical source evidence only in source_records. Do not add source_data or duplicate primary sources in linked_records.external_references.
proposal_rationale: CAM already distinguishes source content from authority, permits read-only and sandboxed security analysis, recognises bounded mandates for coding and security agents, preserves incident evidence, assigns operational incident ownership and supports local or sovereign assurance pathways. The missing connection is a positive defensive-legitimacy and assistance framework. The framework should not create a broad cyber exemption. It should require verified authority and bounded scope, classify the requested assistance, preserve third-party boundaries and confidentiality, and continue with the safest useful mode where execution is not authorised. A provider may still restrict live network action or exploit deployment while allowing timeline reconstruction, indicator extraction, vulnerability explanation, remediation planning, proposed non-executing commands and secure escalation.

proposal_scope.scope_summary: Create a cross-domain Defensive Legitimacy Recognition and Cyber Incident Assistance Framework. SECURITY would define the legitimacy and boundary signals; Annex K would expose runtime-facing assistance postures and target-scope conditions; OPERATIONS would govern incident intake, review, escalation, evidence custody, safe continuation and closure; OPERATIONS-007 would preserve runtime and classifier configuration identity; ARBITRATION would resolve contested authority or target scope; and any future OPERATIONS-008 red-team instrument would cross-reference the transition into a real incident.
registry_components: target, method, time, tool, credential and effect scope
telemetry provenance, custody, sensitivity and retention record
defensive assistance posture and requested action class
classifier, refusal, escalation and review decision
model, runtime, safety-policy and access-tier identity
automation_components: target expansion and third-party boundary check
runtime, cyber-refusal posture and access-tier traceability
interface_components: clear statement of the permitted defensive assistance mode
specific identification of any restricted action or target boundary
narrow confirmation for credentials, live execution or target expansion
non-executing commands, indicators, timelines and remediation guidance where live action is not authorised
local or sovereign continuity option without representing open-weight deployment as inherently safe

suggested_insertion_points: SECURITY-001 — new Defensive Legitimacy Recognition principle: dangerous cyber content does not independently establish malicious intent; distinguish authorised interpretation, reconstruction, validation, containment and remediation from unauthorised operationalisation.

SECURITY-002 — new Defensive Incident Assurance Boundary under or adjacent to the Sovereign Assurance Boundary, covering authority, affected asset, scope, custody, confidentiality, target expansion and alternative local assurance.

Annex K — define runtime-facing defensive-assistance signals and require the narrowest safe useful continuation, including read-only interpretation, indicator extraction, sandboxed validation, remediation planning and proposed non-executing commands.

OPERATIONS-003 — add cybersecurity incident activation and a red-team-to-real-incident transition rule; preserve a single incident owner independent of benchmark or attacker-defender reward objectives.
OPERATIONS-001-SUP-01 — add defensive incident assistance, telemetry custody, classifier decision, access-tier and runtime-configuration fields to logging and audit requirements.
OPERATIONS-001-SUP-02 — add a cyber-content misclassification escalation pathway with bounded human or trusted-security review and time-sensitive incident handling.
OPERATIONS-007 — treat cyber-refusal posture, safety classifier, trusted-access tier, tool/network permissions and local-versus-hosted custody as materially distinct runtime configuration.

ARBITRATION-001 — clarify that defensive purpose, operator authority, affected-system relationship, target, method and requested action must be separately assessed; ownership of an affected system does not create authority over third-party infrastructure.

Future OPERATIONS-008 — cross-reference only: authorised red-team evaluation that causes or discovers real compromise must enter the operational incident lifecycle rather than remain governed solely as an evaluation.
automation_changes: Potential controlled signals and conformance tests must be designed in Caelestis rather than hard-coded as VIGIL-owned canonical codes.
interface_changes: Expose whether the system has classified the request as interpretation, reconstruction, validation, containment, remediation or unauthorised/offensive execution.
Where full assistance is restricted, state the permitted continuation and the specific escalation or authority-review pathway.
Preserve confidentiality, minimisation and custody controls for logs, credentials, personal data, secrets and exploit artefacts.
migration_concerns: Do not create a general exemption for cybersecurity-labelled requests.
Do not infer authority solely from a self-declared role, organisational identity or claim of ownership.
Do not treat ownership of an affected system as authority to attack, disrupt or access third-party infrastructure.
Do not require unrestricted exploit generation, live network execution or credential use as the condition of useful defensive assistance.
Do not equate provider access parity with identical unrestricted offensive and defensive capability; require a justified and operationally usable defensive route.
Do not treat open-weight or local models as inherently safer; preserve binding protections, audit and alternative assurance.
Do not duplicate the red-team capability-cultivation controls proposed by PROP-0019 or the existing incident lifecycle and logging architecture.
dependencies: Human review of the proposed defensive-legitimacy boundary and acceptable evidence of authority.
Surgical Caelestis drafting against the active corpus branch or canonical main if no branch exists.
Coordination with PROP-0019 so evaluation governance and real-incident governance remain separate but interoperable.
Separate legal and sector-specific analysis for incident-response authority, privacy, critical-infrastructure and cross-border data handling.

external_relevance.external_summary: Relevant to model providers, cybersecurity teams, incident-response firms, critical-infrastructure operators, AI safety institutes, regulators and auditors seeking to preserve useful defensive analysis without converting a defensive mandate into unrestricted offensive capability.

resolution_status.resolution_note: Proposal remains open pending human review and coordinated Caelestis amendments. No implemented repair or provider-wide access solution is claimed.

next_action: Draft a coordinated Caelestis amendment package beginning with SECURITY-001, SECURITY-002, Annex K, OPERATIONS-003, OPERATIONS-001-SUP-01 and OPERATIONS-001-SUP-02; then verify OPERATIONS-007 runtime-configuration coverage and add a bounded cross-reference to any future OPERATIONS-008 red-team instrument. Create a PATCH only after adopted wording and verification exist.

review_history.review_scope: Direct review of FM-0048, OBS-0019, PROP-0019 and canonical Caelestis security, boundary-integrity, runtime, incident, logging, escalation and conformance instruments; formulation of a non-duplicative defensive cyber-assistance proposal.
known_limitations: A separate active Caelestis working branch could not be resolved through the available connector; the corpus assessment used canonical main at commit 9917f29e5557e365144c1c3c22f9bc212c470467.
The commercial API providers, exact models, classifier outputs and provider escalation records in the underlying incident remain undisclosed.
No claim is made that open-weight models are categorically safer or that every defensive request should receive live execution capability.
The proposal has not been implemented in Caelestis and does not establish legal authority for any particular cyber operation.
review_history.review_outcome: Existing CAM doctrine provides strong partial coverage but lacks an explicit positive framework connecting defensive authority, cyber-content classification, safe continuation, confidential escalation, runtime identity and incident transition. A distinct proposal is warranted and should remain separate from PROP-0019.
